questions.question_text: A chemist prepares a 90-liter solution by mixing a 15% saline solution with a 40% saline solution. She then performs two operations: first, she removes 20% of the mixture and replaces it with a 60% saline solution; second, she adds 10 liters of pure water. The final mixture has a saline concentration of 28%. What was the quantity (in litres) of the 40% solution in the initial mixture?
questions.solution_text:
Given that the Chemist has a 90-liter solution he made by mixing a 15% saline solution with a 40% saline solution.
Let the initial composition be $x$ litres of 15% saline solution, so, we will have $90-x$ litres of 40% saline solution.
The resulting conc. will be $\dfrac{15x+\left(90-x\right)40}{90}=\dfrac{3600-25x}{90}=40-\dfrac{5}{18}x$
Now 20% of this is taken out i.e. 18 litres and replaced with 60% saline solution.
So, the salt quantity now in the solution is $\dfrac{\left(40-\dfrac{5}{18}x\right)}{100}\times72+\dfrac{60}{100}\times18$
10 litres of pure water is now added, so the total quantity of solution becomes 100 litres.
Given that the saline conc. now is 28%
or, $\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\left(40-\dfrac{5}{18}x\right)}{100}\times72+\dfrac{60}{100}\times18\right)}{100}=\dfrac{28}{100}$
$\left(\dfrac{\left(40-\dfrac{5}{18}x\right)}{100}\times72+\dfrac{60}{100}\times18\right)=28$
$\dfrac{144}{5}-\dfrac{x}{5}+\dfrac{54}{5}=28$
$\dfrac{x}{5}=\dfrac{58}{5}$
$x=58$
58 litres is the quantity of 15% solution in the initial mixture; thus, the quantity of 40% solution = $90-x=90-58=32$ litres.

The non-overlapped region area can be calculated as 
2 * (Area of the rectangle - Area of the overlapped region) = 2 * (104 - 70) = 2 * 34 = 68 $cm^2$

Let the height of the cone be h and slant height be l.
A sphere and a cone have the same curved surface area and share the same radius r.
=> $\pi r^2+\pi rl=4\pi r^2$
=> $l=3r$
Now we know - $l^2=r^2+h^2$
=> $h=2\sqrt{2}r$
The cone is then melted and reshaped into a hemisphere.
=> $\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2h=\dfrac{2}{3}\pi R^3$
=> $\dfrac{1}{3}\pi r^2\left(2\sqrt{2}r\right)=\dfrac{2}{3}\pi R^3$
=> $R=2^{\frac{1}{6}}r$
Thus, the ratio of the total surface area of the hemisphere to that of the sphere will be -
$\dfrac{3\pi R^2}{4\pi r^2}=\dfrac{3\times\ 2^{\frac{1}{3}}\times\ r^2}{4\times\ r^2}=\dfrac{3}{2^{\frac{5}{3}}}$

questions.question_text: Glen borrowed a certain amount from Steve at a compound interest of 20% for two years. Glen invested the money borrowed in a certain ratio in Schemes A and B. He experienced an overall loss of 10% on the money invested in Scheme A, whereas the money invested in Scheme B saw a 50% increase in the same period. What is the ratio of the money invested in both the schemes if he made no profit after two years by paying back the money from the schemes to Steve?
questions.solution_text:
Let the money borrowed by Glen be P. The amount after two years of compounding annually at a rate of 20% becomes,
Money after 2 years = $P\left(1\ +\ \dfrac{20}{100}\right)^2\ =\ 1.44P$
Let the amount invested in Scheme A be aP and the amount invested in Scheme B be bP.
The amount in Scheme A after two years becomes 0.9aP.
The amount in Scheme B after two years becomes 1.5bP.
Since he made no profit, the amount from the schemes must be equal to the money to be paid.
0.9aP + 1.5bP = 1.44P ----(1)
and we also know that a + b = 1 ---(2)
Equation (1) becomes,
0.9a + 1.5b = 1.44  ---(3)
Equation (2) * 0.9 becomes,
0.9a + 0.9b = 0.9  ---(4)
Subtracting (4) from (3), we get,
0.6b = 0.54
$b\ =\ \dfrac{0.54}{0.6}\ =\ \dfrac{9}{10}$
$a\ =\ 1\ -\ \dfrac{9}{10}\ =\ \dfrac{1}{10}$
Ratio = $a\ :\ b\ =\ \dfrac{1}{10}\ :\ \dfrac{9}{10}\ =\ 1\ :\ 9$
Hence, the correct answer is option B.

questions.question_text: A wine shop seller uses a peculiar price-change scheme to sell his goods. He buys a 20-litre bottle of wine, increases its price by p% and later reduces the new price again by p%. After one such price-change cycle, the price of the bottle decreased by £ 15 and after the second price-change cycle, the price of the bottle stood at £ 48. At what price did the wine shop seller buy the wine bottle?
questions.solution_text:
Let $C$ be the cost price of the wine before the price change. After one cycle of price change, a reduction equal to  $C\left(\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)$ takes place. It is stated that this value is  £ 15.
$C\left(\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)=£15$...........(i)
Let the price after the reduction be $C'$; then: $C\left(1-\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)=C'\ or\ \left(C-15\right)=C'$
After the second round of price change, we obtain:$C'\left(1-\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)=£48$
We can re-write this as: $\left(C-15\right)\left(1-\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)=48$
Replacing $\left(\frac{p^2}{100^2}\right)$ from (i), we get: $\left(C-15\right)\left(1-\frac{15}{C}\right)=48\ or\ \left(C-15\right)^2=48C$.....(ii)
We can simplify this as $C^2-78C+225=0$ and on solving, we get $C=£75$ [Cost price].
Hence, Option A is the correct choice.

questions.question_text: A and B move toward each other on a straight 150-meter track, with speeds of 2 m/s and 4 m/s, respectively. The moment they meet, a third person, C, starts from A's starting point and moves toward B's end at 7 m/s. After how many seconds will C be equidistant from both A and B (other than the point when C is starting)?
questions.solution_text:
A and B move toward each other on a straight 150-meter track, with speeds of 2 m/s and 4 m/s, respectively. Thus they will meet after 150/(2+4) = 25 seconds
Now, after they meet, C start from the same end as A, and moves towards the other end. Speed of C is 7 m/s. Let us assume that C is equidistant from both A and B after T seconds.
Total distance covered by A from A's end = $2(T+25)=2T+50$
Total distance covered by B from A's end = $150-4(T+25)=50-4T$
Total distance covered by C from A's end = $7T$
Now, the distance between A and C = $\left|5T-50\right|$, and the distance between B and C = $\left|11T-50\right|$. And, it is given that C is equidistant from both A and B. Thus, -
$\left|5T-50\right|=\left|11T-50\right|$
Case - 1 : $5T-50=11T-50$ => $T=0$ seconds. This is the time when A and B meet, and C started. But we have to find the time other than the point when C started.
Case - 2 : $5T-50=-11T+50$ => $16T=100$ => $T=6.25$ seconds.

questions.question_text: What is the least number that should be multiplied with 15! so that the product is a perfect square?
questions.solution_text:
We know that $10!=2^8\times3^4\times5^2\times7^1$
Extending 10! to 15!:
$15!=10!\times11\times12\times13\times14\times15$
$15!=2^8\times3^4\times5^2\times7^1\times11\times\left(3\times2^2\right)\times13\times\left(7\times2\right)\times\left(5\times3\right)$
Or, $15!=2^{11}\times3^6\times5^3\times7^2\times11\times13$
Now, we know that for sum to be a perfect square, all its prime factors should have an even number of power. 
However, we have, 2, 5, 11 and 13 that has an odd number of power.
If we multiplied 15! with the product of 2, 5, 11 and 13, we will get the even powers for all four. 
Hence, the least number that should be multiplied with 15! to get a perfect square: $2\times5\times11\times13=1430$

questions.question_text: Lewis and Max are racing in the opposite direction on a straight road of length $168$ km. After meeting, Max takes $108$ minutes and Lewis takes $\dfrac{100}{3}$ minutes to reach the other end. Find the speed of the faster person (in km/hr).
questions.solution_text:
Since Lewis and Max are racing in opposite directions on a straight road, we can use the formula for the time it takes them to meet.
The formula is: 
Meeting Time = square root of the product of time taken by the two persons to reach the respective ends after meeting
$=\sqrt{\ 108\times\ \dfrac{100}{3}}=\sqrt{\ 3600}=60$ minutes
So, total time for Lewis will be $=\dfrac{100}{3}+60=\dfrac{280}{3}$ minutes
Total time for Max will be $=108+60=168$ minutes
Clearly, Lewis takes less time to complete the race
So, he is the faster racer
So, speed of faster racer (Lewis) = Distance/Time = $\dfrac{168}{\dfrac{\dfrac{280}{3}}{60}}=\dfrac{168\times\ 60}{\dfrac{280}{3}}=108$ km/hr.
Alternate Explanation:
We also have another formula to find the ratio of speeds of Lewis and Max.
Ratio of their speeds = square root of the inverse ratio of time taken to reach other end after meeting.
Let, speed of Lewis be $S_L$ km/hr and speed of Max be $S_M$ km/hr
So, $\dfrac{S_M}{S_L}=\sqrt{\dfrac{\ \dfrac{100}{3}}{108}}=\sqrt{\ \dfrac{100}{3\times\ 108}}=\sqrt{\ \dfrac{25}{81}}=\dfrac{5}{9}$
From this we can infer, Lewis is the faster racer.
Also, we can say until meeting, distance covered by Max and Lewis is in the ratio 5:9
So, distance covered by Lewis until meeting = $\dfrac{9}{5+9}\times\ 168=\dfrac{9}{14}\times\ 168=108$ km
Meeting time (we calculated in the previous part)=60 minutes = 1 hour
So, speed of Lewis (faster runner)=$\dfrac{108}{1}=108$ km/hr.
